title.narrative: Strengthening Inclusive Governance and Gender-Responsive Fisheries Management

description.narrative: The project responds to the interconnected challenges of biodiversity loss, unsustainable artisanal fisheries, and weak community governance in Inhambane Province. Coastal and marine ecosystems are increasingly threatened by overfishing, habitat degradation, climate change, and poverty. Artisanal fisheries, which sustain most local livelihoods and contribute significantly to national fish production, face declining productivity and high post-harvest losses, undermining food security and income stability. Further, mangrove degradation exacerbates ecosystem vulnerability, while limited capacity of Community Fisheries Councils (CCPs), weak coordination, and inequitable participation hinder effective community-based management. These issues are intensified by widespread poverty, food insecurity, and climate risks that disproportionately affect women and marginalized groups. Expected Achievements The project will benefit coastal communities in Inhambane Province, especially artisanal fishers, women, and youth dependent on marine and mangrove resources. It aims to: • Strengthen inclusive and participatory governance of fisheries and coastal ecosystems through capacity building, coordination platforms, and gender-equity tools. • Enable communities to co-develop and enforce sustainable resource management rules, fostering equitable participation and reducing conflicts. • Improve post-harvest handling, processing, and cold-chain systems to minimize food losses, improve nutrition, and enhance market opportunities. • Support participatory mangrove mapping and restoration to boost coastal protection, biodiversity, and carbon storage while promoting community stewardship. Collectively, these actions will enhance food security, diversify livelihoods, and strengthen resilience to climate and environmental shocks, contributing to sustainable and equitable coastal resource management in Inhambane Province.
